We act for Ms. Sayedehmaryam Alavinasab ("Maryam"), who we believe is likely the victim
of a Ponzi scheme operated by Mr. Seyed Mohammed Ali Nojoumi, Smart Prime Group Ltd.,
Smart Prime Group Inc., (together "Smart Prime") and Ms. Behnaz Samavat, Mr. Nojoumi's
wife. We believe Mr. Amir Mostoufi is also part of the scheme.
Maryam was born in Iran on September 21, 1978. She is a Canadian citizen who has been
living in Canada since June 2019 with her husband and two daughters. She has a Masters
in Industrial Mechanical Engineering and currently works as an interior designer.
Mr. Nojoumi is the CEO of Smart Prime Group. He was previously charged in 2019 with
fraud over $5,000 and possession of property obtained by crime, although the charges
appear to have been withdrawn in February of 2022. A news article relating to Mr. Nojoumi's
prior charges is attached at Tab 1. Mr. Nojoumi lives at 18 Apple Orchard Path in Thornhill
Ontario, with his wife, Ms. Samavat, and their son.
Smart Prime Group Ltd. is incorporated in St. Vincent and Grenadines. Smart Prime Group
Inc. has been incorporated in Ontario since July 17, 2020. A copy of Smart Prime Group
Inc.'s Ontario registration is attached at Tab 2.
Maryam was not aware of Mr. Nojoumi's prior legal issues and she was not aware that
Ontario securities laws require investment businesses like Smart Prime to comply with
registration requirements.
Maryam's Investment with Smart Prime
Shortly after she moved to Canada, Maryam began attending a private gym called Ultra
Fitness. Around two years ago, Maryam met a man named Mr. Amir Mostoufi at Ultra
Fitness, and they became friends. She learned that Mr. Mostoufi, and Mr. Nojoumi , who also
attended Ultra Fitness, were involved in the stock market and in crypto currencies.
Anna Perschy, Ontario Securities Commission — May 31, 2023

Approximately one year ago, Mr. Mostoufi began promoting Smart Prime to Maryam,
explaining that it was an asset management company that had interesting opportunities for
investors. Mr. Mostoufi mentioned that some of Maryam's friends had been investing their
money with Smart Prime for years and achieved excellent results.
Mr. Mostoufi arranged a meeting with Maryam at Smart Prime's office in Toronto in
September 2022. Mr. Nojoumi was also present at the meeting. Mr. Mostoufi explained that
he was a partner with Smart Prime, and that Mr. Nojoumi was the president. Maryam recalls
being shown a presentation about investing with Smart Prime, which included the
information that Smart Prime was created 12 years ago, had over 80 investors, and
managed over USD$50 million. Maryam also recalls being shown a spreadsheet with Smart
Prime's investors, who appeared to be located in Ontario. Two photos taken of this
spreadsheet can be found at Tab 3.
Maryam was told that Smart Prime would need to clear her information before she could
invest with them. Maryam subsequently filled out a form with her information. Two days
later, Maryam was informed that her information had been cleared and she could begin
investing with Smart Prime. She was told the minimum investment was $300,0000SD. Mr.
Mostoufi and Mr. Nojoumi recommended that she invest $350,000USD in a fixed rate
investment and $50,000USD in a variable investment program.
On October 7, 2022, Maryam transferred $549,200CAD to Smart Prime, and on November
7, 2022, she transferred a further $300,00CAD. Maryam wired both installments from her
personal bank account at CIBC. At Mr. Mostoufi's instruction, Maryam wired the first
installment ($549,200CAD) to a Bank of Montreal account in the name of Georgia Holiday
Inc. Maryam was informed by Mr. Mostoufi that this was because of exchange rates as
Smart Prime would have to pay double the exchange rates if she sent her money directly to
them. She wired the second installment ($300,00CAD) to a CIBC bank account in the name
of 13987124 Canada Inc., at Mr. Nojoumi's instruction. Copies of the wire confirmations for
both transfers are attached at Tab 4. Copies of Mr. Mostoufi and Mr. Nojoumi's text
messages instructing Maryam where to send her funds are attached at Tab 5. Note, the text
messages are currently being translated into Engl ish.
On October 13, 2022, Maryam entered into a Managed Account Authorization Agreement
with Smart Prime Group, allowing Ali Nojoumi to purchase and sell securities on Maryam's
behalf. Maryam signed a further Managed Account Authorization on November 14, 2022.
Both agreements provided for a guaranteed 24% yearly return. A copy of the authorizations
are attached at Tab 6.
In December of 2022, Mr. Mostoufi called Maryam and informed her that Smart Prime would
be bringing their shares to Nasdaq but needed to raise 12 Million dollars to do so. Over a
two week period, Mr. Mostoufi and Mr. Nojoumi called Maryam on multiple occasions asking
her to invest further funds. On December 16, 2022, she wired $300,000CAD to Smart
Prime. At Mr. Nojoumi's instruction, she sent the wire to a Desjardins bank account in the
name of Georgia Holiday Inc. A copy of this wire transfer is attached at Tab 4.
On January 4, 2023, Maryam entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement with Smart Prime. A
copy of this agreement is attached at Tab 7.
Mr. Nojoumi explained to Maryam that all of her investments would be deposited by Smart
Prime into its omnibus account with Advanced Markets LLC. Maryam was never provided
with any documentation confirming that her investments were actually deposited with
Anna Perschy, Ontario Securities Commission — May 31, 2023

Advanced Markets LLC. Advanced Markets LLC appears to be a Bermuda-based entity that
facilitates trading for its clients.
Smart Prime Ceases to Pay the Guaranteed Monthly Returns
While Maryam initially received the guaranteed monthly returns of 2% on her investments,
the last payment she received was on March 27, 2023. In total she received three payments
from Smart Prime, all delivered in cash by Mr. Mostoufi: on November 18, 2022, Maryam
received $9,300CAD; on January 18, 2023, Maryam received $15,000CAD; and on March
27, 2023, Maryam received $30,000CAD. Since then, Maryam has not received any of the
guaranteed monthly returns on her investments. She has tried to contact Mr. Mostoufi to
inquire about her payments, but he refused to answer his phone.
On May 8, 2023, Mr. Mostoufi approached Maryam at Ultra Fitness and told her that Smart
Prime was having problems and would not be able to pay her until the problems were
resolved.
Maryam subsequently learned that a family friend of hers, Mr. Alireza Saeed, had also
invested with Smart Prime at the encouragement of Mr. Mostoufi, and was no longer
receiving any of the guaranteed monthly returns on his $5,904,505USD investment. Mr.
Saeed is currently represented by a different lawyer.
Maryam and Mr. Saeed approached Mr. Nojoumi on multiple occasions to inquire about the
status of their investments and why they were no longer receiving their returns. Mr. Nojoumi
explained that Advanced Markets LLC had frozen the investment funds of Smart Prime as
neither he, nor Smart Prime, had the required licenses to trade securities.
Maryam and Mr. Saeed have now learned of three other individuals, in addition to Mr.
Mostoufi, who had invested with Smart Prime and are no longer receiving any of their
guaranteed returns. These individuals are Alireza Onghaei, Gholamreza Zarmehr, and
Niyousha Falaknazi.
On May 9, 2023, Mr. Saeed met with Mr. Nojoumi and Ms. Samavat at the Smart Prime
office at 9201 Yonge St., Unit 102, Richmond Hill, Ontario, L4C 6Z2. Mr. Saeed asked Mr.
Nojoumi to sign an acknowledgement outlining the terms to which Mr. Saeed invested with
Smart Prime, as well as the debt owed to Mr. Saeed. A copy of this acknowledgement is
attached at Tab 8.
On May 16, 2023, Mr. Saeed, Maryam, and the other identified investors met with Mr.
Nojoumi and Ms. Samavat at 9201 Yonge St., Unit 102, Richmond Hill, Ontario, L4C 6Z2.
The investors requested that Mr. Nojoumi , Ms. Samavat, and Smart Prime sign an
acknowledgement of the debt owed to them. The total debt acknowledged was
$10,976,484USD. The total debt owed to Maryam was $868,222USD. The
acknowledgement also stated that Smart Prime had not paid the guaranteed return to any of
the named investors from January 15, 2023 onwards, and stated that Smart Prime would be
making efforts to have the funds directly returned to the investors from Advanced Markets
LLC. Mr. Nojoumi signed the acknowledgement personally and on behalf of Smart Prime,
but Ms. Samavat refused to do so. A copy of the executed acknowledgement is attached at
Tab 9.
On May 22, 2023, Maryam attended an investors meeting at Smart Prime which was held at
9201 Yonge St., Unit 102, Richmond Hill, Ontario, L4C 6Z2. The other investors named in
the acknowledgement dated May 16, 2023, also attended the meeting. At the meeting, Mr.
Anna Perschy, Ontario Securities Commission — May 31, 2023

Nojoumi announced that Smart Prime was shutting down their brokerage accounts with
Advanced Markets LLC due to Smart Prime's failure to obtain licensing. Mr. Nojoumi
requested that clients submit a formal withdrawal request to Smart Prime to initiate the
return process for their investments. A copy of the meeting minutes are attached at Tab 10.
A copy of the Smart Prime's Statement of Work with Advanced Markets LLC is attached at
Tab 11.
Mr. Nojoumi has provided no subsequent updates to Maryam regarding the return of her
funds.
On May 30, 2023, Maryam was informed by Mr. Saeed that Advanced Markets LLC had
emailed Smart Prime indicating that it had initiated the liquidation process. Photos taken of
this email are attached at Tab 12.
Maryam now believes that Mr. Nojoumi has absconded with her investment proceeds and
fears that Mr. Nojoumi could flee Canada. Maryam requests the Ontario Securities
Commission, the Joint Serious Offences Task Force, and RCMP investigate Mr. Nojoumi
and Smart Prime and hopefully locate her investment proceeds.

Swap rates (also known as the "cost of carry") are the interest rate differential between each of
the currencies in a currency pair displayed as, and embedded in, currency trades. Whilst swap
rates primarily depend on the interest rate differential, they also reflect expected deviations in
interest rates, the period/tenor of the swap, exchange rate fluctuations, market events, volatility
and liquidity.
Each currency pair trades to a "spot value date" which may be one day or two days from the
current trade date (T+l or T+2) depending on the pair traded. Each day at 5pm ET, the value
date moves forward to the next viable value date for each pair, taking into account holidays in
either of the currencies in the pair. Rolling over a position to a new value date, results in either a
credit or a debit to an account to finance the carrying forward of any position still open at 5pm
ET. The side (long or short) and size of the position as well as bank holidays will determine the
cost or return of the rollover interest. Generally, being "long" the currency with the higher
interest rate will result in a credit and vice versa. The Swap rates used are based on market prices
from Tier-1 banks.
Our swap rates are applied each day at 5:00pm ET as this is the end of the current trading day
and the time when spot value dates are \rolled forward. Trades that have been opened before
5:00pm ET, and held open past that time; will be subject to swap rates.
Swap rates for currencies that settle on trade date plus 2 are tripled on Wednesday at 5:00pm to
account for weekend days (the value date moving from a Friday to a Monday). For currencies
that settle on trade date plus 1, swap rates are tripled on Thursday to account for weekend days.
This is the standard structure for swap rate application. However, when a holiday occurs on a
potential value date/settlement date, the swap rate is altered to account for the holiday, which
could result in no interest cost/return or an additional cost/return.
Swap rates are visible in Fortex Back Office under Settlement Reports. By clicking on the
"Swap Rates" section, you will be directed to the swap rates for all currency pairs in USD based
on a 10K position.

Swaps in Fortex 5 Platform/ Advanced

Swap rates (also known as the "cost of carry") are the interest rate differential between each of
the currencies in a currency pair displayed as, and embedded in, currency trades. Whilst swap
rates primarily depend on the interest rate differential, they also reflect expected deviations in
interest rates, the period/tenor of the swap, exchange rate fluctuations, market events, volatility
and liquidity.
Each currency pair trades to a "spot value date" which may be one day or two days from the
current trade date (T+l or T+2) depending on the pair traded. Each day at 5pm ET, the value
date moves forward to the next viable value date for each pair, taking into account holidays in
either of the currencies in the pair. Rolling over a position to a new value date, results in either a
credit or a debit to an account to finance the carrying forward of any position still open at 5pm
ET. The side (long or short) and size of the position as well as bank holidays will determine the
cost or return of the rollover interest. Generally, being "long" the currency with the higher
interest rate will result in a credit and vice versa. The Swap rates used are based on market prices
from Tier-1 banks.
Our swap rates are applied each day at 5:00pm ET as this is the end of the current trading day
and the time when spot value dates are \rolled forward. Trades that have been opened before
5:00pm ET, and held open past that time; will be subject to swap rates.
Swap rates for currencies that settle on trade date plus 2 are tripled on Wednesday at 5:00pm to
account for weekend days (the value date moving from a Friday to a Monday). For currencies
that settle on trade date plus 1, swap rates are tripled on Thursday to account for weekend days.
This is the standard structure for swap rate application. However, when a holiday occurs on a
potential value date/settlement date, the swap rate is altered to account for the holiday, which
could result in no interest cost/return or an additional cost/return.
Swap rates are visible in Fortex Back Office under Settlement Reports. By clicking on the
"Swap Rates" section, you will be directed to the swap rates for all currency pairs in USD based
on a 10K position.
